evidence.text: Q3 2026 market data put existing-home transaction volume up about 7-9% yoy and prices down about 7%. In Q2 Beike's platform resale orders grew 25% against a 20-city market growing about 10%, and its existing-home GTV rose 8.0%. Against the Q3 2025 base of RMB505.6bn existing-home GTV and RMB5.99bn revenue, that supports existing-home GTV of roughly +3% to +10% and revenue on the line up low-to-mid single digits. That is broadly what a -5.8% total revenue consensus already assumes for transactions.

evidence.text: Profit run-rate looks above the EPS bar. Q2 2026 adjusted net income was RMB3,185m (adjusted EPS $0.42), with gross margin 28.6% (+6.7pt), adjusted operating margin 14.6% and GAAP opex down 14%. In 2025, Q3 adjusted net income (RMB1,286m) was 0.71x Q2's (RMB1,821m). Applied to Q2 2026 that gives about RMB2.25bn, or about $0.29-0.30 per ADS, against a $0.23-0.25 consensus (year-ago $0.16 adjusted) and a $0.30 whisper. The renovation contraction is 'basically complete' and margins rose in every segment. The downside: the CFO said not to extrapolate one quarter's profit, Q2 carried a RMB280m bad-debt provision on SINIC receivables that could recur, and new-home receivables risk persists.

If the market priced the run-rate, consensus would sit at the $0.30 whisper and the stock would not have fallen 5.7% in the week before the print. The EPS bar is disputed ($0.21-$0.25), so the size is capped.

A 1-percentage-point first-home mortgage interest subsidy for new and resale homes took effect 1 October 2026. Resale makes up about 27% of qualifying first-tier transactions vs 7.8% for new homes, so it skews to Beike's existing-home business. New-home sales stayed weak (-13% in 30 cities).

Management confirming October-November platform volumes (company-level, not the 20-city proxy) is the unpriced part.

evidence.text: The new-home line is a drag. Beike's new-home revenue (RMB6.64bn in Q3 2025, about 29% of revenue) faces a weak market: 100-city new-home sales -7% yoy in August, 30-city new-home area -13% in October, and an 28 August policy package that pushes presale toward completed-home sales and hit developer stocks (HK developers index -6.2%). Beike's Q2 new-home GTV was only +1.2% with resources concentrated on premium projects. Net of the rest: existing-home and rental margins are rising, so this hits revenue more than profit (new-home contribution margin 28.8%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: new-home GTV -13.7% and revenue -14.1%, yet the stock rose about 7% premarket on margins/buyback. This name has looked through new-home weakness before.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus revenue already falls 5.8%. The residual is that new-home GTV could print negative again against a +1.2% Q2, which previews do not highlight (the finviz preview mentions only 'new-home demand weakening').

evidence.text: Through H1 the company booked $43.9m of revenue (Q1 $20.9m, Q2 $23.0m). The FY2026 guide of $99-103m therefore needs H2 of $55.1-59.1m, about $27.5-29.5m a quarter, against a Q2 run-rate of $23.0m. The Q2 10-Q says HEMOBLAST Bellows supply from sole manufacturer Dilon (France) covers expected sales only 'through the end of Q3 2026', is 'uncertain' after that, and Dilon can terminate on 30 days' notice. With Q3 consensus at $25.5-27.1m, Q4 would need about $29-33m, so a second guide cut or a soft Q4 framing on 2026-11-16 is likely. Street FY consensus is still about $102m and Q4 about $30.1m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-11 a 7% revenue miss plus a $2m FY guide trim ($101-105m to $99-103m) gave -28.89% on the day. On 2026-05-13 a guide raise to $101-105m with the HEMOBLAST deal gave -4.0%. Guidance changes have moved this name hard to the downside.
evidence.why_not_priced: Estimates are not reset. Aggregators still carry FY about $102m and Q4 about $30.1m from 2 analysts, above even the lower guide midpoint, and both analysts rate the stock Buy. If the guide were seen as broken, consensus would sit near or below $97m. Partly priced: the stock is down 41% since the 2026-08-10 close ($0.446 to $0.264) and sits at its 52-week low. The supply caveat lives in a 10-Q risk passage, not in the press release.
evidence.independence: The FY guide and H1 figures are in the Q2 and Q1 press releases (https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/XTNT/xtant-medical-reports-q2-2026-financial-results; https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1899732/xtant-medical-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results). The Q4 consensus of $30.1m is from https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XTNT/earnings-forecasts. The supply wording is single-source (the 10-Q). Peer biologics softness (separate finding) also points to a guide cut.

evidence.text: Orthobiologics peers that reported after Xtant last spoke had a soft Q3 2026. Alphatec (2026-10-29) said Q3 biologics revenue fell about $1m YoY on lower biologics attachment, cut its FY guide, saw thoracolumbar market growth slow to low single digits, and expects flat biologics into Q4. Bioventus (2026-11-02) cited 'softness in Bone Graft Substitutes', reported elsewhere as about -6%. Orthobiologics were 75% of Xtant's Q2 revenue ($17.4m), and management had promised biologics acceleration in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Biologics shortfall was the stated cause of the 2026-08-11 guide cut (-28.89%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus Q3 of $25.5-27.1m implies a $2.5-4m sequential step-up. That assumes the promised biologics acceleration plus HEMOBLAST, and it does not reflect peer softness reported 2-3 weeks after the estimates were last set. If priced, Q3 estimates would sit at or below $25m. This is a proxy: Xtant sells through independent agents and has 25 new reps, so its own share gains could offset the market.
evidence.independence: Bioventus Q3 release, 2026-11-02: 'softness in Bone Graft Substitutes' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001665988/000166598826000050/bioventusex-991q32026.htm). Globus US spine +2% only (https://finviz.com/news/417606/globus-medical-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-and-announces-a-500-million-increase-to-the-share-repurchase-program). All are proxies. Net of the rest of the company: spinal implants are about 25% of revenue (~$5.7m), flat-ish after the divestiture, and do not offset.

evidence.text: Liquidity and covenant pressure. At 2026-06-30 the company had $9.9m cash (down from $17.3m at year-end), $23.0m of debt, and only $0.7m available on the revolver. H1 operating cash flow was -$9.4m. MidCap Amendment No. 5 (2026-08-10) waived a Q2 minimum orthobiologics revenue covenant breach, reset the covenant levels (not disclosed), and raised term-loan amortization by $0.15m from Q4 2026 and $0.3m a quarter after that. Q3 is the first test of the reset covenant. The money funds operating losses and the HEMOBLAST sales force, not a corroborated revenue ramp. Management told Canaccord (2026-08-11) it expects to generate cash and need no more capital by Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior print where financing was the surprise. The August print, with a covenant waiver disclosed in the 10-Q, fell 28.9%, but the guide drove that.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the market cap is about $37m against $23m of debt, at a 52-week low. What is unpriced is whether Q3 needs another waiver or a raise, or whether the 'cash generation by Q4' claim holds. Neither is visible until the release and 10-Q. If a raise were priced, the stock would have gapped on an 8-K or S-3. EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-08-11 and no shelf. Financing question answered: the money covers losses under covenant pressure, which is the negative case, so the sign is negative but small.
evidence.independence: Management's cash-generation claim cuts the other way (https://quartr.com/events/xtant-medical-holdings-inc-xtnt-canaccord-genuity-s-46th-annual-growth-conference_oSup1xgB). This finding shares the 10-Q document with the guide finding but rests on different numbers (balance sheet and covenant, not revenue run-rate).

evidence.text: HEMOBLAST Bellows changes how it is booked in Q3. In Q2 Xtant acted as agent and booked only $1.3m net of Dilon's fulfilment costs. Management said sales would exceed $1m a month on a GROSS basis as the transition to Xtant contracts completes, and the 10-Q says supply covers sales through the end of Q3. So Q3 headline revenue gets a mechanical lift of about $1.5-2m+ from the switch to gross alone, before any biologics growth.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the first quarter with HEMOBLAST at gross, so there is no history. Revenue beats on this name have been bought: +13.6% on 2025-08-12 and +15.4% on 2025-05-12.
evidence.why_not_priced: Probably mostly in the two-analyst consensus, which already steps Q3 up to $25.5-27.1m. The disputed bar caps this finding. If the market had read the gross step-up as a clean beat, the stock would not be making new lows into the print.
evidence.independence: The 10-Q gives the agent-versus-principal note and the Q3 supply coverage (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1453593/000149315226036981/form10-q.htm). This is the same HEMOBLAST product as the guide finding, but it points the other way for the reported quarter only. The two are consistent: Q3 gets lifted, Q4 is at risk.

It expects the 2027 framework to be broadly similar, so there is no relief for Xtant's amnio line.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Amnio headwinds were a named cause of the 2026-08-11 guide cut (-28.89%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company already named it in the August guide cut, so it lands inside what was guided. Filed small because the peer confirms there was no Q3 recovery.
